area: Mission Center GIS explorer (statewide Event Groups -> incidents -> evidence). Source of truth: web/src/features/missionCenter/MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx (page + aside), web/src/features/missionCenter/MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx (ArcGIS map + legend), web/src/features/missionCenter/missionCenterGisModel.ts (types/helpers), web/src/components/mapTheme.ts (basemap), web/src/components/MissionCenterMap.tsx (unrouted legacy). All paths relative to C:\ERIS-worktrees\eris-design-system. Routes are registered in web/src/App.tsx:95-118 via web/src/pages/MissionCenterPage.tsx (a bare re-export). Role gate is in-component (isOperationalUser, MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:225) and server-side (backend/app/routes/mission_center_event_groups.py:20 require_roles(OPERATIONAL_ROLES)).

screens.name: Statewide Event Groups (PROJECTS mode)
screens.purpose: Show every California Event Group as a marker on one map with a searchable/filterable card list so an operational user can find and open the group they care about.
roles: (route itself is only ProtectedRoute at web/src/App.tsx:95-102; gating is isOperationalUser at web/src/features/missionCenter/MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:225 using web/src/utils/roleModel.ts:17-38; nav entry only for operational users at web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:84)
primaryTasks: Locate an Event Group geographically (by district/county/route or by scanning the map) and drill into it
Get a statewide pulse: how many groups are open and how many incidents are active
Filter groups by status (Open/Closed/Archived) and by free-text search

responsive.layout: AppShell (px-4 md:px-6; sidebar only at lg, otherwise a 'Navigation' card stacked above the content) > page 'grid gap-4 p-4 md:p-5' > toolbar (flex-wrap) > 'grid items-start gap-4 xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,2fr)_minmax(340px,0.8fr)]' holding the map card (height clamp(540px, calc(100vh - 320px), 900px)) and an aside 'flex max-h-[760px] flex-col overflow-hidden'. Below xl (1280 px) map and aside stack vertically, map first.
breakpointsUsed: AppShell: sm:flex (theme select), md:block (user name), md:px-6, lg:flex-row / lg:hidden / lg:block (sidebar) (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:140-165)
No sm/lg/2xl, no overflow-x-auto, no min-w in the Mission Center files; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx uses no breakpoints at all
phoneRisks: 375 px: content width is ~309 px (shell px-4 + page p-4 + card border). The search/select grid has flex-basis 340 px and grid-cols-[minmax(220px,1fr)_auto]; 220 px input floor + ~110 px select + 8 px gap ≈ 338 px > 309 px, so the toolbar overflows horizontally with no overflow-x handling (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:242-244).
The 'Navigation' card for <lg renders above the page content (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:164), so ~10 nav links push the toolbar and map below the first screen.

Map min height is 540 px (clamp floor) regardless of viewport (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:283); on an 812 px-tall phone the Event Group list is a full screen below the map and the user must scroll past a map that captures touch-pan.
Aside has its own max-h-[760px] scroll region inside the page scroll (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:286) — nested scrolling on touch.
Refresh button is px-2.5 py-1.5 text-xs (~28 px tall) — under the 44 px touch target guideline (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:255).
Map click both opens a popup and navigates; on touch there is no hover preview so a mis-tap on a cluster of 11 px markers changes the route (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:196-205, 251).
Summary strip and 'Updated …' text wrap onto multiple lines at text-xs, which is fine, but the ml-auto right-alignment collapses into a left-aligned second row.
tabletRisks: 768–1024 px is still below xl, so the map and the aside stack; on a 1024×768 landscape tablet calc(100vh-320px)=448 px which clamps up to 540 px, so the map takes the whole viewport and the list starts off-screen (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:271, 283).
The aside's max-h-[760px] is taller than a landscape tablet viewport; the list scroll region and page scroll compete.
At 768 px the toolbar fits (search grid 340 px + summary text wraps under it).
desktopNotes: ≥1280 px: two-column 2fr/0.8fr with the aside floored at 340 px; map up to 900 px tall vs aside capped at 760 px so bottoms do not align (items-start).
AppShell caps content at max-w-[1900px]; at that width the map is ~1100 px wide and the marker popups stay small (dockEnabled:false, MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:183).
Sidebar collapse (w-64 -> w-16) gives the map ~190 px more (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:165).

painPoints.issue: Every 60 s auto-refresh (and every search keystroke / status change) creates a new projects array, which re-runs the marker effect and calls view.goTo(CALIFORNIA_EXTENT), snapping the map back to the statewide view and discarding the user's pan/zoom.
painPoints.evidence: MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:148, 157-161, 203-207 (new array identity) -> MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:229-263 (effect deps [mode, projects, selectedProjectId], line 262 goTo)

painPoints.issue: Marker popup content is dead: clicking a marker navigates in the same click handler, so 'Click the marker to inspect this Event Group.' and the popup fields are never read; on touch there is no way to peek at a group without leaving the statewide view.
Search/status toolbar overflows horizontally on a 375 px phone because of the 220 px minmax floor plus an auto-width select inside a 340 px flex basis.
Map is forced to ≥540 px tall and sits above the card list, so on phones/tablets the accessible fallback list (the only keyboard-reachable navigation) is a full screen below the fold.
Two different counts are shown with no explanation of the difference: the toolbar totals are unfiltered while the aside says '{n} shown on map' for the filtered set.
Legend explains marker size but not the three status colours (blue/slate/light-slate), so Closed vs Archived is undecodable on the map.
Loads the entire statewide dataset (up to 100 pages × 1000 groups) on every 60 s tick even while the user is drilled into an incident where the group layer is not rendered.
painPoints.evidence: MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:139-147, 157-161; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:234 (early return in non-PROJECTS mode)

painPoints.issue: Popup shows raw enum 'Status: OPEN' while the cards show 'Open'; ArcGIS Search widget and the app's search box are both labelled 'Search' with different meanings.
Non-numeric or zero :gid in the URL silently falls back to PROJECTS mode without a 404 or notice.

strengths: Deep-linkable, route-driven state: mode is derived purely from URL params so browser back/forward and shared links work (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:119-130).

Cursor pagination follows has_more/next_cursor with a guard against a non-advancing cursor, so the statewide view is never silently capped (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:139-147; backend/app/routes/mission_center_event_groups.py:15-61).

Cards and markers are two synchronized entry points to the same navigation, giving keyboard/screen-reader users a non-map path (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:296; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:211-213 comment).
Theme-aware basemap swap (topo/dark-gray with an API key, OSM fallback without) observed via data-theme MutationObserver (web/src/components/mapTheme.ts:16-34).
Map is constrained to California with minZoom 5, so users cannot get lost off-state (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:28-34, 182).
Stacking-context guard keeps ArcGIS DOM from painting over app overlays (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:374; web/src/index.css:120-124).
Clear, specific empty/loading copy and a role=alert error banner (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:268, 295).

screens.name: Event Group drill-down (PROJECT mode)
screens.purpose: Zoom the map to one Event Group's incidents and list them with status and classification so the user can pick the incident whose GIS evidence they need.
roles: Same operational set as /mission-center (MAINTENANCE_COORDINATOR, GEOTECH_OFFICE_CHIEF, GEOTECH_BRANCH_CHIEF, GEOTECH_ENGINEER, REVIEWER, ADMIN and their legacy aliases) — route is ProtectedRoute at web/src/App.tsx:103-110, gate at MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:225
primaryTasks: See where a group's incidents sit relative to each other and which are still active
Pick an incident to inspect its GIS evidence
Jump to the full Event Group workspace (/event-groups/:id) for history and assessments

entryPoints: 'View on Mission Center map' on Event Group detail (web/src/pages/EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:78)
Breadcrumb group-title link and '← Event Group Incidents' from the incident level (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:262, 334)

responsive.layout: Identical shell to the statewide mode: breadcrumb bar (flex-wrap) replaces the search toolbar; map card then aside, side by side only at xl.
phoneRisks: Long group titles wrap in the breadcrumb, pushing the ml-auto location label to a third line (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:259-265).

Aside header stacks back button + eyebrow + title + id/location + three pills + description + full-width link (≈260 px) before the incident list begins, all below a ≥540 px map (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:309-317).
Back button is text-[11px] px-2 py-1 (~22 px tall) — well under the 44 px touch target (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:310).
Diamond markers are 13 px with a 2 px outline; adjacent incidents in one group are hard to tap distinctly, and a tap navigates immediately (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:291-293, 206-210).
Card hover affordance (hover:border/hover:bg) is the only visual hint that cards are buttons; no focus-visible ring is declared (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:321).
tabletRisks: Stacked layout below 1280 px: map (≥540 px) then a 760 px-max aside; a user comparing marker positions to the list must scroll back and forth.
Undocked popups (dockEnabled:false) on a 768 px-wide map obscure neighbouring markers when opened by a stray tap (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:183).
desktopNotes: Works well at ≥1280 px: markers and cards visible together; view.goTo(graphics) fits all incidents (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:303-306).
When the group has zero incidents the map centres on the group centroid at zoom 13 with an empty map and no on-map message (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:305).

painPoints.issue: Classification label falls back to 'Loading classification…' permanently when /incident-classifications/query fails or returns no row for an incident, so a failure reads as an in-progress load.
painPoints.evidence: web/src/features/incidents/incidentClassification.ts:19; MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:174-182 (setError also nulls eventGroupDetail on any failure), 324

painPoints.issue: A deep link whose incident GIS loads but whose incident is not in the group's incident list leaves the aside blank: mode becomes INCIDENT (only incidentGis is checked) but the INCIDENT block requires selectedIncident, and neither fallback message at 390/391 matches.
Incident marker popup is unreadable in practice because the click navigates; the 'Click the marker to inspect GIS evidence.' sentence is dead copy.
Legend omits the orange In-progress diamond and mislabels the red diamond as 'Active' when the code distinguishes NEW (red) from IN_PROGRESS (orange).
No search or status filter for incidents within a group; the toolbar disappears once drilled in (large groups become a long unfiltered card list).
Redundant navigation and labels: back button duplicates breadcrumb; 'Selected Event Group' eyebrow; group location shown twice (breadcrumb right side and aside).
Red 'bad' tone on the '{m} active' pill signals an error state for what is simply a count; the same count uses neutral text on the statewide cards.
Any failure in the group-detail effect sets eventGroupDetail to null, which flips the aside to 'Event Group #{id} was not found.' even for transient network errors.

strengths: Map auto-fits to the group's incidents (view.goTo(graphics)) so the first view is always useful (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:303-306).
Classification is loaded for all incidents in one POST rather than per card (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:174-177).
Direct link to the fuller Event Group workspace keeps Mission Center a read-only GIS lens rather than duplicating the workspace (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:316).
Async effects use a cancelled flag so stale responses cannot overwrite a newer selection (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:166-188).
Consistent StatusPill component with semantic tones reused across all three levels (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:80-89).

screens.name: Incident GIS evidence (INCIDENT mode)
screens.purpose: Show one incident's saved affected-area geometry and geotagged field photos (with camera-heading wedges) on the map, with a synchronized evidence list, so a reviewer can verify where the evidence was captured.
roles: Same operational set (MAINTENANCE_COORDINATOR, GEOTECH_OFFICE_CHIEF, GEOTECH_BRANCH_CHIEF, GEOTECH_ENGINEER, REVIEWER, ADMIN + aliases) — route ProtectedRoute at web/src/App.tsx:111-118; gate MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:225; backend require_roles(MISSION_CENTER_ROLES) at backend/app/routes/mission_center_gis.py:186-190
primaryTasks: Verify photo evidence locations and camera headings against the incident location and saved geometry
Check evidence coverage (how many photos are mapped / have heading / are unmapped)
Jump to the technical submission, the incident record, or the Event Group workspace

Evidence list is far below the map: header (~200 px) + facts + tiles + description + actions precede the photo list, all after a ≥540 px map, so the map/list sync (the feature's point) requires scrolling between them on every photo.
tabletRisks: Stacked layout: tapping a photo row scrolls nothing — the map (above) recentres off-screen; the user has to scroll up to see the effect (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:372-373 does not scroll the map into view).

The 760 px aside scroll region plus 540–900 px map exceed a portrait tablet's height; the notice banner sits above the grid and can be off-screen when it appears (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:269).
desktopNotes: At ≥1280 px the list-to-map sync is excellent: click a row, map zooms to ≥17 and opens the popup (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:144-159).
The aside can still overflow its 760 px cap with many photos while the map is up to 900 px; two independent scroll heights.
Only the selected incident is drawn, so users cannot hop to a neighbouring incident from the map (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:272-274).

painPoints.issue: On any viewport below xl the map and the evidence list are not visible together, defeating the click-row-to-focus-map interaction; nothing scrolls the map into view after focusPhoto.

Photo correction/provenance data (location_overridden, heading_overridden, horizontal_accuracy_m, location_source, heading_source) is fetched but not shown, so a reviewer cannot tell a corrected heading from a device heading.
Raw values leak into the UI: 'Saved geometry: MultiPolygon' and popup 'Captured: 2025-03-01T14:22:10Z' while the list formats the same timestamp.
Breadcrumb's right-hand location label is the Event Group's, not the incident's, at incident level.
The notice banner lives above the map grid, far from the photo row that triggered it, and never auto-dismisses except when another mapped photo is focused.
Photo row thumbnails use alt='' and the row's only accessible name is the visible file name; the mapped/unmapped meaning of a click is conveyed only via a title tooltip (hover-only).
Legend does not include the selected-incident diamond marker that remains on the map in INCIDENT mode.

Three inconsistent labels for the same destination across two levels: 'Open full Event Group workspace' vs 'Open Event Group'; and 'Open in Incidents' vs the Incidents page's 'View on map' reverse link.

strengths: List-to-map sync through a small imperative handle (focusPhoto) with a graceful fallback for unmapped photos and an explanatory notice (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:36-39, 144-159; MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:372-376).

Camera-heading wedge geometry is shared with the submission evidence map (headingWedgeRing, PHOTO_HEADING_WEDGE_FILL_ALPHA), so reviewers see the same visual language in both places (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:21, 337-343; web/src/components/SubmissionArcGisMap.tsx:511-528).

Accent colour for photo evidence is read from the CSS theme variable with a fallback, so markers follow light/dark/coastal themes (web/src/components/photoEvidenceGraphics.ts:56-64; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:324).
Popup HTML is escaped (escapeHtml) before interpolating user-controlled file names and URLs (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:54-61, 328-334).

Backend reuses the quality-gated submission photo-map when a submission exists and falls back to incident photos otherwise, so the view works during coordinator review (backend/app/routes/mission_center_gis.py:192-224).
Full GeoJSON coverage (Polygon, MultiPolygon, LineString, MultiLineString, Point, MultiPoint, GeometryCollection) so any saved geometry renders (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:75-108).
Coverage tiles (Photos/Mapped/Heading/Unmapped) give an instant evidence-quality read before scrolling the list (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:350-354).

screens.name: Mission Center GIS map panel (shared across all three modes)
screens.purpose: Single ArcGIS MapView that re-symbolizes five graphics layers according to the current mode and exposes standard GIS widgets plus a mode-specific legend footer.
roles: Rendered only for operational users (parent gate at MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:225)
primaryTasks: Pan/zoom to find and select Event Groups or incidents by clicking markers
Switch basemap, toggle layers, geocode a place with the ArcGIS Search widget

dataShown.label: Basemap: topo-vector (light) / dark-gray-vector (dark) with VITE_ARCGIS_API_KEY, otherwise OSM
dataShown.note: Theme-aware only when a key is configured; 'coastal' theme falls to topo (mapTheme.ts:16-19 only checks 'dark').

dataShown.label: Five GraphicsLayers titled 'Event Groups', 'Event Group incidents', 'Saved incident geometry', 'Camera headings', 'Field photos' (visible in LayerList)
dataShown.note: Titles are user-facing in the LayerList; empty layers still appear.

dataShown.label: Home, Compass, dual-unit ScaleBar
dataShown.note: Standard; Home returns to the initial California extent.

dataShown.label: Expand buttons with tooltips 'Search map', 'Basemaps', 'GIS layers'
dataShown.note: Tooltips are hover-only (ArcGIS Expand); icons are the only visible affordance.

dataShown.label: Legend footer (mode-specific chips)
dataShown.note: Hand-drawn CSS swatches approximate the symbols; incomplete in every mode (see pain points).

dataShown.label: aria-label 'Mission Center Event Group and Incident GIS explorer' on the map div
dataShown.note: Label without a role or tabindex; ArcGIS injects its own focusable canvas.

actions.label: Click marker (PROJECTS: group; PROJECT: incident)
actions.note: Single view.on('click') with hitTest; mode read from a ref (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:196-214).

exits: Marker clicks drive route changes through onSelectProject/onSelectIncident callbacks

responsive.layout: Wrapper 'map-stack-guard overflow-hidden rounded-xl border' with a div whose height is a prop (Explorer passes clamp(540px, calc(100vh - 320px), 900px); component default 650 px) and a flex-wrap legend footer.
breakpointsUsed: None in MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx; height comes from the parent prop (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:283); legend uses flex-wrap (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:376)
phoneRisks: Fixed-min 540 px height consumes ~66% of a 812 px phone viewport; ArcGIS captures single-finger pan so the page is hard to scroll past the map.
Three Expand buttons + Home + Compass at ArcGIS default 32 px on a 309 px-wide map crowd the top edge; the Search widget when expanded is wider than the map.
popup dockEnabled:false means popups float over the small map; the photo popup contains a 320 px image (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:183, 329).
Legend chips wrap into 2–3 rows under the map on narrow widths (fine, but adds height).
tabletRisks: At 768–1024 px the map is full-width; the 5-layer LayerList and BasemapGallery panels open at ArcGIS default widths (~300 px) over the map — usable.
Home widget resets to the statewide extent even when drilled into an incident (Home stores the initial viewpoint), which is disorienting at incident level (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:186).
desktopNotes: snapToZoom:false and minZoom 5 give smooth zoom within California (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:182).
Effects call view.goTo with duration 0 — no animation, which makes the auto-recentre on refresh feel like a glitch rather than a transition (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:262, 304, 367).

painPoints.issue: Legend is incomplete in every mode: statewide omits Closed/Archived colours; group level omits the orange In-progress diamond; incident level omits the selected-incident diamond.
Home widget returns to the statewide extent rather than the current drill level, and the three goTo calls use duration 0, so re-centres feel like jumps.
Theme-aware basemap only when VITE_ARCGIS_API_KEY is set; without it every theme gets OSM, and the 'coastal' theme is treated as light.
Map markers are not keyboard-operable and there is no on-map text alternative; the cards are the only accessible route (acknowledged in a code comment).
LayerList shows all five layers regardless of mode, so users can toggle empty layers and be confused when nothing changes.

strengths: One MapView instance for all three modes (no remount on drill), keeping ArcGIS init cost to once per page (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:161-227).
Callbacks and mode are held in refs so the single click handler never goes stale without re-subscribing (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:134-141).
Clean teardown: click handle removed, view destroyed, refs nulled (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:217-226).
Symbol sizing carries meaning consistently (selected > active > resolved/idle) across levels (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:251, 291).

screens.name: Access notice for non-operational users
screens.route: /mission-center, /mission-center/:gid, /mission-center/:gid/:iid (same routes; rendered when isOperationalUser is false)
screens.purpose: Tell a maintenance-reporting account that Mission Center is not available to them.
roles: MAINTENANCE_FIELD_WORKER / MAINTENANCE (maintenance-only accounts) and any signed-in user with no operational role (web/src/utils/roleModel.ts:16, 36-44; MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:225-235)
primaryTasks: Understand why the page is empty and go somewhere useful

dataShown.label: Message: 'Mission Center is available to ERIS operational engineering and coordination roles. Maintenance reporting accounts remain scoped to their own reports.'
dataShown.note: Explains the restriction; no next step is offered.

dataShown.label: AppShell header, nav card/sidebar (without a Mission Center entry), footer
dataShown.note: Nav still gives a way out; the page title 'Mission Center' is shown for a page the user cannot use.

entryPoints: Direct URL or a shared /mission-center/... deep link (the nav item is hidden for these users at web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:84)
exits: Global sidebar nav only (typically Incidents, Settings)

phoneRisks: None specific; short text block.
desktopNotes: Panel is full content width with no max-width, so the two sentences stretch across ~1500 px at 1900 px.

painPoints.issue: Gating is inconsistent with sibling operational pages: /event-groups, /assessments and /gis/* use RoleRoute (which redirects to /submissions), while Mission Center uses ProtectedRoute plus an inline message with no link out.

Backend returns 403 for the same users (require_roles OPERATIONAL_ROLES), so if the client gate ever disagrees with the server the user sees a generic 'Failed to load' banner rather than this explanation.

strengths: Message states the rule in plain language and names who is scoped where (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:230).
The fetch is short-circuited for non-operational users so no 403 noise reaches the console (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:133).

crossCutting: Vocabulary: code still speaks 'Project' (MissionCenterMode 'PROJECTS'/'PROJECT', ProjectSummary, groupToMapProject/detailToMapProject, selectedProjectId, projectLocationLabel, incidentGis.project) while the UI says 'Event Group'; the adapter fakes project_uuid from event_group_key (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:31-33, 35-68; missionCenterGisModel.ts:5-27; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:24-25, 43-45). Backend keeps a parallel legacy /mission-center/projects endpoint (backend/app/routes/mission_center_gis.py:163-183) beside the live /mission-center/event-groups.

Vocabulary: the same screen is called 'Mission Center' (nav + <h1>), 'California Event Groups' (breadcrumb root), 'Event Groups' (aside header), 'All California Event Groups' (back button) and 'Event Group Incidents' (incident-level back button) (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:84; MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:227/238, 260, 290, 310, 334). 'open' is used for groups and 'active' for incidents in the same sentence (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:252); 'incidents' pill is lowercase while every other label capitalizes 'Incidents' (314 vs 299, 319).

Duplicated helpers: eventGroupLocationLabel and projectLocationLabel are byte-identical, as are eventGroupStatusLabel and projectStatusLabel (web/src/features/eventGroups/eventGroupTypes.ts:71-85 vs web/src/features/projects/projectTypes.ts:98-112); the Explorer imports the former and the map imports the latter for the same data (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:9; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:25).

Duplicated map code: CALIFORNIA_EXTENT is declared twice (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:28-34; web/src/components/MissionCenterMap.tsx:25-31); photo marker + heading wedge drawing is implemented separately in MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:326-358 and web/src/components/SubmissionArcGisMap.tsx:493-548 with different marker sizes (11 vs 9 px), attribute names (photoId vs attachment_id) and popup content builders.

Dead/legacy code: web/src/components/MissionCenterMap.tsx is not imported anywhere (grep hits only its own definition) — an unrouted, OSM-only, water-drop-marker predecessor. missionCenterGisModel.ts exports MissionCenterProjectPage, mappedPhotos, headedPhotos and classificationForIncident that only the test file uses (missionCenterGisModel.ts:5-9, 58-64, 81-86; missionCenterGisModel.test.ts). detailToMapProject copies the events array the map never reads (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:55-66; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx never touches projectDetail.events). backend /mission-center/incidents feed (backend/app/routes/incidents.py:2075) is not called by the web app.

Inconsistent button styles: each page redefines its own btn/btnPrimary string with different padding/weight (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:91-92 px-3 py-2 font-semibold; web/src/pages/EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:29 font-medium + disabled:opacity-50; web/src/features/submissions/SubmissionDetailHeader.tsx:26; web/src/features/assessments/AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:126-127 py-1.5 text-xs). Within Mission Center alone there are four button sizes: 11 px back buttons (310, 334), 12 px Refresh (255), 14 px btn/btnPrimary (91-92), and full-width card buttons. A .btn-brand utility exists in web/src/index.css:87-95 but is unused here.

Inconsistent status rendering: StatusPill is local to the Explorer (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:80-89) while EventGroupDetailPage uses EventGroupStatusBadge; incidentStatusLabel (76-78) vs incidentStatusText on EventGroupDetailPage:126; formatTimestamp (70-74) vs formatDate elsewhere; map popups print raw enum codes ('OPEN', 'IN_PROGRESS') and raw ISO timestamps while the aside prints humanized labels (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:243, 257, 284, 297, 333).

Map recentre-on-data-change: derived arrays with fresh identity (eventGroups -> mapProjects -> visibleMapProjects) feed ArcGIS effects that call view.goTo, so the 60 s poll and every filter keystroke reset the viewport. Any future consumer of MissionCenterProjectGisMap inherits this unless the effect separates 'data changed' from 'mode changed' (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:148, 203-207; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:229-263).

Accessibility gaps: breadcrumb is a div with <b> for the current item (no <nav aria-label='Breadcrumb'>, no aria-current) (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:259-265); section labels are styled divs, not headings (290, 311, 319, 335, 365); loading/notice text has no aria-live (269, 295, 320, 342); interactive cards and photo rows have hover-only affordances and no focus-visible styles (296, 321, 369-378); the photo-row intent is conveyed by a title tooltip (378); back buttons and Refresh are below 44 px touch height (255, 310, 334); the map's only accessible name is an aria-label on a div with no role (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:375); marker colour is the only encoding of status on the map (63-73) with an incomplete legend.

Responsive pattern: the whole area uses only md:p-5 and one xl: grid; nothing addresses the 640–1279 px band, and the map's clamp floor (540 px) plus the aside's max-h-[760px] are fixed pixel values that do not scale with viewport (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:239, 271, 283, 286). The AppShell's <lg 'Navigation' card stacks above content (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:164), which is especially costly for a map-first page.

Route gating: Mission Center routes are wrapped in ProtectedRoute with an in-component role check (web/src/App.tsx:95-118; MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:225), whereas /event-groups, /assessments and /gis/terrain-cross-sections use RoleRoute (web/src/App.tsx:61-94, 119-126). Two gating patterns for one role set.

Polling: a statewide fetch of every Event Group (up to 100 × 1000 rows) runs every 60 s for the life of the page regardless of mode, and clears the shared error slot each tick (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:133-161). There is no visibility check (document.hidden) and no cancel on unmount for an in-flight page loop.
